items.title: Section: Mindfulness of the Breath Opens — the Fifth Purifying Object

items.zh: 云何阿那波那念所緣？謂緣入息、出息念，是名阿那波那念。此念所緣入出息等，名阿那波那念所緣。
items.en: What is the object of mindfulness of the breath? … Mindfulness that takes the in-breath and out-breath as its object is called mindfulness of the breath. What this mindfulness takes as its object — the in-breath, the out-breath, and so on — is called the object of mindfulness of the breath.

items.title: In-Breath and Out-Breath, and the Subtle Interval Between

items.zh: 當知此中，入息有二。何等為二？一者、入息，二者、中間入息。出息亦二。何等為二？一者、出息，二者、中間出息。入息者，謂出息無間，內門風轉，乃至臍處。中間入息者，謂入息滅已，乃至出息未生，於其中間在停息處，暫時相似微細風起，是名中間入息。如入息、中間入息，出息、中間出息，當知亦爾。此中差別者，謂入息無間，外門風轉，始從臍處，乃至面門、或至鼻端、或復出外。
items.en: Know that here, the in-breath is twofold. What are the two? The in-breath itself, and the mid-interval in-breath. The out-breath is likewise twofold: the out-breath itself, and the mid-interval out-breath. The in-breath is: immediately following the out-breath, wind turns inward through the inner gate, moving from the face and nose down to the navel. The mid-interval in-breath is: once the in-breath has ceased, and before the out-breath has yet arisen, in that interval, at the point of rest, a faint and subtle wind-like motion briefly arises — this is called the mid-interval in-breath. The out-breath and its mid-interval should be understood the same way, with this difference: immediately following the in-breath, wind turns outward through the outer gate, moving from the navel up to the face, or to the tip of the nose, or beyond, out of the body.

items.title: What Makes Breath Possible: Karma, Body, and Mind Together

items.zh: 入息、出息有二因緣。何等為二？一、牽引業；二、臍處孔穴，或上身分所有孔穴。入息、出息有二所依。何等為二？一、身，二、心。所以者何？要依身心，入出息轉，如其所應。若唯依身而息轉者，入無想定、入滅盡定、生無想天諸有情類，彼息應轉。若唯依心而息轉者，入無色定、生無色界，彼息應轉。若唯依身心而轉，非如其所應者，入第四靜慮，若生於彼諸有情類，及羯羅藍、頞部曇、閉尸等位諸有情類，彼息應轉。然彼不轉。是故當知，要依身心，入出息轉，如其所應。
items.en: The in-breath and out-breath have two conditions. What are the two? A drawing karma, and the cavity at the navel or the cavities of the upper body. … The in-breath and out-breath have two supports. What are the two? The body, and the mind. Why is this? Because the breath moves in dependence on both body and mind, as is fitting to each case. … If breath moved on the strength of the body alone, then beings in the attainment of no-perception, the attainment of cessation, and those born in the heaven of no-perception would still breathe. If breath moved on the strength of mind alone, then those in a formless absorption, or born in the formless realm, would still breathe. If breath moved simply because body and mind are both present, without regard to what is actually fitting, then those in the fourth absorption, or born there, and beings at the stages of the embryo's earliest weeks, would still breathe. Yet in none of these cases does breath move. Therefore know: breath moves in dependence on both body and mind, precisely as is fitting to each case.

items.zh: 入息、出息有二種行。何等為二？

items.title: Two Loci, Four Names for the Breath

items.zh: 一者、入息向下而行；二者、出息向上而行。入息、出息有二種地。何等為二？一、麁孔穴，二、細孔穴。云何麁孔穴？謂從臍處孔穴乃至面門、鼻門，復從面門、鼻門乃至臍處孔穴。云何細孔穴？謂於身中一切毛孔。入息、出息有四異名。何等為四？一名風，二名阿那波那，三名入息出息，四名身行。風名一種，是風共名；餘之三種，是不共名。
items.en: First, the in-breath travels downwards; second, the out-breath travels upwards. The in-breath and out-breath have two loci. What are the two? The coarse cavity, and the subtle cavity. What is the coarse cavity? It is the passage from the navel's cavity up to the face and nose, and from the face and nose back down to the navel's cavity. What is the subtle cavity? It is every pore throughout the body. The in-breath and out-breath have four other names. What are the four? First, wind; second, ānāpāna; third, in-breath and out-breath; fourth, bodily activity. "Wind" is the shared name, common to all kinds of wind; the other three are names unique to the breath alone.

items.title: Two Faults in Practice: Too Lax, Too Forced

items.zh: 修入出息者有二過患。何等為二？一、太緩方便，二、太急方便。由太緩方便故，生起懈怠，或為惛沈睡眠纏擾其心，或令其心於外散亂。由太急方便故，或令其身生不平等，或令其心生不平等。云何令身生不平等？謂強用力持入出息。由入出息被執持故，便令身中不平風轉。由此最初於諸支節皆生戰掉，名能戰掉。此戰掉風若增長時，能生疾病。由是因緣，於諸支節生諸疾病。是名令身生不平等。
items.en: There are two faults in cultivating mindfulness of the breath. What are the two? Practising too laxly, and practising too forcefully. Through practising too laxly, laziness arises; the mind becomes entangled in dullness and drowsiness, or else becomes scattered outward. Through practising too forcefully, either the body or the mind becomes thrown out of balance. What is it for the body to become thrown out of balance? It is forcibly seizing hold of the breath. Because the breath is being forcibly controlled, an unbalanced wind arises within the body. From this, at first, trembling arises in the limbs and joints — this is called "trembling." If this trembling wind increases, it can produce illness. Through this condition, various afflictions arise in the limbs and joints — this is called the body becoming thrown out of balance.

items.title: Section: The Two Faults Close; Five Modes of Cultivation Named

items.zh: 云何令心生不平等？謂或令心生諸散亂，或為極重憂惱逼切。是名令心生不平等。又此阿那波那念，應知略有五種修習。何等為五？一、算數修習，二、悟入諸蘊修習，三、悟入緣起修習，四、悟入聖諦修習，五、十六勝行修習。
items.en: What is it for the mind to become thrown out of balance? It is either the mind giving rise to various kinds of scattering, or the mind being pressed by extremely heavy anxiety and distress. This is called the mind becoming thrown out of balance. … Know that this mindfulness of the breath, briefly stated, has five modes of cultivation. What are the five? First, cultivation through counting; second, cultivation through realising the aggregates; third, cultivation through realising dependent origination; fourth, cultivation through realising the noble truths; fifth, cultivation through the sixteen excellent practices.

items.title: Counting the Breath: Two of Four Methods

items.zh: 云何名為算數修習？謂略有四種算數修習。何等為四？一者、以一為一算數，二者、以二為一算數，三者、順算數，四者、逆算數。云何以一為一算數？謂若入息入時，由緣入出息住念，數以為一。若入息滅，出息生，出向外時，數為第二。如是展轉數至其十。由此算數非略非廣，故唯至十。是名以一為一算數。云何以二為一算數？謂若入息入而已滅，出息生而已出，爾時總合數以為一。即由如是算數道理，數至其十，是名以二為一算數。
items.en: What is cultivation through counting? Briefly, there are four methods of counting. What are the four? First, counting one for one; second, counting two as one; third, counting forward; fourth, counting backward. What is counting one for one? When the in-breath enters, attending to it with mindfulness that rests on the in-breath while the out-breath is stilled, one counts it as one. When the in-breath has ceased and the out-breath arises and moves outward, one counts it as two. Continuing this way, one counts up to ten. This count is neither too brief nor too long, and so goes only to ten. This is counting one for one. What is counting two as one? When the in-breath has entered and ceased, and the out-breath has arisen and gone out, at that point the two together are counted as one. Continuing by this same method up to ten — this is counting two as one.

items.zh: 入息、出息說名為二，總合二種數之為一，故名以二為一算數。

blocks.text: The fifth purifying object, **mindfulness of breathing** (ānāpānasmṛti), for those dominated by discursive thought. This is one of the most detailed accounts of breath meditation in Indian Buddhist literature.
"Mindfulness that takes the in-breath and out-breath as its object."

In-breath and out-breath each have a "mid-interval": "once the in-breath has ceased, and before the out-breath has arisen, a faint breath" remains. Venerable Miào Jìng: it rests there without moving, yet there is breath there too.

Two conditions: a karma that draws the life on, and the body's cavities. Two supports: body and mind. "If breath moved on the strength of the body alone, beings in the attainments without perception or in cessation would still breathe"; breath needs both.

The in-breath goes down, the out-breath up. Breath passes through "coarse cavities" (mouth and nose) and "subtle cavities": "every pore throughout the body". Master Cháng Bǎi: that is why we feel wind and heat on the skin. Four names: wind, ānāpāna, in-and-out breath, bodily activity.

"Practising too laxly, and practising too forcefully." Too lax: laziness, drowsiness, scattering. Too forced: "forcibly seizing hold of the breath" throws the body out of balance, and the mind into anxiety. Venerable Miào Jìng: let the breath be natural.

Five ways of practice: counting, realising the aggregates, realising dependent origination, realising the truths, and the sixteen excellent practices. Counting has four methods: one breath as one, two breaths as one, forward, backward. "This count is neither too brief nor too long, and so goes only to ten."

quiz.q: What is mindfulness of the breath, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 波那?
options: mindfulness taking in- and out-breath as object; 波那 means carrying out — carrying in and out
quiz.why: "Mindfulness that takes the in-breath and out-breath as its object is called mindfulness of the breath." Venerable Miào Jìng: 波那 means "carrying away" — carrying in and carrying out.

quiz.q: What is the mid-interval in-breath, and why don't beginners notice it, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: after the in-breath ceases and before the out-breath arises, a faint wind-like motion at the pause; one must calm the mind to sense it
quiz.why: "Once the in-breath has ceased, and before the out-breath has yet arisen, in that interval, at the point of rest, a faint and subtle wind-like motion briefly arises." Master Cháng Bǎi: beginners may practise long without knowing it, because the mind must be still to sense it.

quiz.q: What are the two conditions of the breath, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "drawing karma"?
options: drawing karma, and the navel or upper-body cavities; past karma draws forth the breath
quiz.why: "A drawing karma, and the cavity at the navel or the cavities of the upper body." Venerable Miào Jìng: drawing karma is karma you created in past lives, whose drawing power causes you to have in- and out-breath.

quiz.q: The text says if breath depended on body alone, beings in the heaven of no-perception would breathe. How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe that heaven?
options: a lifespan of five hundred great eons spent in absorption — no breath, though the body remains
quiz.why: "If breath moved on the strength of the body alone, then beings in the attainment of no-perception, the attainment of cessation, and those born in the heaven of no-perception would still breathe." Venerable Miào Jìng: throughout a lifespan of five hundred great eons they stay in absorption with no breath, though the body is there.

quiz.q: What is the breath's "subtle cavity," and how does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it?
options: every pore of the body — wind feels cold and heat seeps in everywhere
quiz.why: "What is the subtle cavity? It is every pore throughout the body." Master Cháng Bǎi: when wind blows you feel cold, and heat seeps in through the subtle cavities, everywhere on the body.

quiz.q: What faults come from practising too laxly, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi sum up the two faults?
options: laziness, dullness and drowsiness, or outward scattering; one is too slack, the other too earnest — both excess and deficiency are faults
quiz.why: "Through practising too laxly, laziness arises; the mind becomes entangled in dullness and drowsiness, or else becomes scattered outward." Master Cháng Bǎi: one is too unserious, the other too serious; neither is right — too much and too little both bring faults.

quiz.q: Counting one-for-one is "neither too brief nor too long," so only to ten. What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: counting just one-two is too brief and leads to sleep; Miào Jìng cites Zhiyi: count only the out- or only the in-breath
quiz.why: "This count is neither too brief nor too long, and so goes only to ten." Master Cháng Bǎi: counting one-two, one-two, you'll soon fall asleep — too brief. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you count out-breaths, don't count in-breaths, and vice versa — count only one of the two.
